pathogen_derived_negatives.why: Original negatives came from only 2 lab strains while positives spanned 45 organisms, so organism and hazard labels were ~96% correlated and the baseline AUROC could not be attributed to hazard. These are benign cytoplasmic metabolic and DNA-repair proteins from the SAME pathogens that supply the positives, which breaks that correlation.
pathogen_derived_negatives.selection: Function held fixed, organism varied. Reviewed UniProt entries only. Fragments excluded. Deliberately EXCLUDED: enolase and GAPDH (moonlighting adhesins in pathogens), GroEL and DnaK (same concern), proteases, pilins and cell-wall synthases, any of which can be virulence-associated.

second_batch_2026_09_03.query_fix: organism_id matches exactly and does NOT include strain descendants; most reviewed entries are tagged at strain-level taxid. Switching to organism_name free text recovered 7 of 11 failures. Same root cause as the earlier Pseudomonas aeruginosa 287 vs PAO1 208964 case.

rejected_taxonomic_drift.Bacillus amyloliquefaciens: only reviewed hits are Bacillus velezensis (strain FZB42 reclassified). JK decision: leave orphan.

second_batch_2026_09_03.retroactive_verification: All 51 fetched entries were re-checked against the rule 'the requested species name must appear in the returned OS= field'. 50/51 passed. The first pass had no such filter; it was added only for the retry and is now applied retroactively.

maintenance_notes: 2026-09-04: counts.negative_blocks was stale (still described the 50-negative panel) and is recomputed here from the entries themselves. Added lab-strain / pathogen-derived / unflagged tallies because the localization control now has to filter on lab_strain to stay organism-controlled.

2026-09-04: added 54 secreted benign proteins from pathogen organisms (block secreted_pathogen) so the exported half of the doubly controlled localization test is no longer empty. Species verification applied on the FIRST pass this time. Rejections: {'collides_with_positive_class': 33, 'blocked_protein_name': 2, 'species_mismatch': 9, 'duplicate_accession': 1}.

2026-09-05: added 14 non-homologous members to classes with n < 7 (adp_ribosyl 3->7, rip 3->7, superantigen 4->7, clostridial 4->6, contact_dependent 3->4) so small-n classes carry enough members to distinguish class recovery from single-member accidents. Every candidate was screened at Smith-Waterman <= 0.30 against existing members AND against already-accepted candidates. counts.positive_final moves 66 -> 80; positive_raw/positive_dedup still describe the original FASTA build. Class eligibility is UNCHANGED: an earlier version of src/23 recomputed holdout_eligible_classes as n >= 3, which promoted the other_toxin_mechanism grab-bag into the results table and flipped virulence_associated_non_toxin from its deliberate non-mechanism-control flag; both are reverted here. Screened 39 candidates; rejections: {"duplicate_sequence": 1, "homologous_to_a_candidate_already_accepted": 4, "homologous_to_existing_member": 11, "name_lacks_own_class_vocabulary": 9}.
